sources.title: E-Government: Djibouti eVisa
sources.publisher: E-Government Portal / National Agency for State Information Systems, Republic of Djibouti
sources.officialityEvidence: The current E-Government portal says administrative information is certified and validated by relevant administrations and identifies ANSIE as a public agency attached to the Presidency. Its eVisa guidance describes approval, email delivery, printing, and replacement of the point-of-entry visa.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Une fois que la demande est approuvée, l'eVisa est envoyé au demandeur par courrier électronique.

sources.title: National Tourist Office: entry formalities
sources.officialityEvidence: The live National Tourist Office page directs visitors to the government eVisa site but also identifies embassy and consular channels. It supplies no nationality schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Les visiteurs peuvent obtenir leur visa électronique (eVisa) en soumettant leur demande en ligne.

sources.title: Djibouti Immigration eVisa: terms and eligibility framing
sources.officialityEvidence: The active gouv.dj service redirects to its live applicant site. Its terms say the service is owned and operated by the Republic of Djibouti and concerns foreign nationals subject to a visa, but name neither eligible nationalities nor ordinary-passport exclusions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: This website is owned and operated by the Republic of Djibouti; it informs nationals of any foreign country subject to a visa.

sources.title: Law No. 201/AN/07/5ème L: entry and stay conditions
sources.publisher: Official Journal of the Republic of Djibouti
sources.officialityEvidence: The Official Journal publishes the enacted entry law. Its foreign-entry baseline is expressly subject to international conventions, bilateral agreements, and special regimes, without a nationality schedule.
sources.supportingExcerpt: sous réserve des conventions internationales et des accords bilatéraux.
